translation:
The One-Grass Pavilion and the Secretly Transmitted Ophthalmology, each in one volume, were engraved by Lord Nian Ouzhai Xiyao of Guangning in the Kangxi reign. As the years have passed, the original books are rarely seen, and what circulates is for the most part hand copies. Recently the Shenbao Press printed them with movable type, but the number of copies was limited, and without the plates they could not be reprinted. Those who were somewhat late in purchasing the book could not obtain it. The various formulas in the book, having been followed and applied in treatment over the years, have shown remarkable effects, and I have several times wished to print it to spread its transmission. In the winter of the gengzi year, I returned to my village to avoid the war, and met my maternal uncle, Mr. Xu Dingweng. In the course of conversation we found we were of one mind. Thereupon, following the example of share certificates, we together solicited contributions, gathered funds, and reprinted this book. Not only do the sick and blind gain the joy of again beholding the sun and sky, but this book is thereby transmitted, and all who rely on it obtain a basis, by which they may illuminate it with divine understanding and gradually attain a long life. How small is what is preserved? This is my preface.

<ins>Respectfully written by Yao Baoxin, styled Bochun, of Jiaxing, in the first ten days of the second month of the xinchou year of the Guangxu reign</ins>
translator_notes: 申報館 (Shenbao Press) was a Shanghai newspaper that did movable-type printing.
股份票 (share certificates) refers to stock certificates.
上浣 (shanghuan) means the first ten days of the month.
